assessment: The observed first-drop and warning windows do not support a long known-self-wake wait or a sampled endpoint-mutex wait spike as their immediate explanation. External readiness is untimed, mutex phases are sampled, and no unique cause or ordinary ranking follows.
limits: Every poll entry/self-wake is traced; only every 64th poll has phase/detail counters and at most eight route batches plus one rotating selected queue send. Unselected counters remain unavailable.
Known-ready waiting intervals refer only to instrumented self-wakes; other readiness sources are not timestamped. Their retained-window time fraction is not CPU duty or executor starvation.
Receive/event Pending includes cooperative suspension. Receive/event budget exits record rescheduling reasons and do not prove remaining source backlog.
Acquisition/send intervals are elapsed time including descheduling. A small sampled acquisition does not establish absence of contention outside those samples.
UDP cumulative deltas require identical PID, owned-inode set, and UDP socket count; onset is bounded by actual read samples, never an exact packet-loss timestamp.
Warning alignment uses printed UTC precision and start/drop monotonic brackets, assuming no unobserved realtime clock step. The warning timestamp is not the exact refusal-instruction time.

The collector requests 4 ms UDP and 40 ms per-TID reads. Actual gaps/collection time, recorder clock/TLS/ring work, ring allocation and post-run dump are diagnostic costs; no ordinary CPU/RSS/latency/throughput comparison is valid.
The failed run has no measured gate, so actual generated work and generation lag are unavailable; the planned offer cannot substitute for actual completed work.
The six-attempt full-history series has five passes then one refusal; it is a new 32x-row-storage diagnostic experiment and is not ranked against the earlier 8192-row series.
Ready/measured/done events have no absolute/monotonic timestamp, and observer rows have no gate marker. Exact offer/drain/cleanup boundaries cannot be reconstructed.

For passing runs only, source order proves offer start S>=0 and measured gate before endpoint Drop D. Measured elapsed E therefore bounds S<=D-E. The common fixed-offer core [D-E,4s] is conservative source-derived coverage, not an observed gate timestamp.

First UDP-drop wall intervals use observer outer wall timestamps through collector completion, translated by the envelope of trace anchor offsets. Floating wall-clock precision and unobserved realtime steps limit this alignment.
Processing/wait partitions clip global non-overlapping intervals before summation. Sampled phase totals are kept in a separate domain and never extrapolated to elapsed wall duty.
